summary: Audit Press + Watch Tower codebase for reusable monitoring/control capabilities (status, logs, restart) before designing a live control-panel UI

result.headline: ~75% reuse: Press already has the service-status, per-service log, and restart primitives — the board is mostly an aggregator + a Vue page + two thin wrappers (per-service restart, Watch-Tower JSON), not a rebuild.
result.reuse_pct_estimate: ~75% reuse / ~25% new build. Reuse: all data sources (supervisor status, logs, restart, ping, Prometheus usage, server/bench/site enumeration) and all UI building blocks (DevOverview layout, ObjectList badge-theme table, LogViewer drawer, confirmDialog, run_doc_method bridge). New build: one batched server→bench→service aggregator endpoint, one whitelisted per-service supervisorctl restart wrapper, a Watch-Tower→JSON status adapter for host-level disk/redis/mariadb/docker/microservice/agent probes, dashboard wrappers for the 6-7 ungated deploy_flow/ping methods, the server→bench→service tree page + service-row component, and auto-poll/caching.

reuse_map.ui_need: List all servers (top tier of the tree)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: list of App+DB servers {name,title,status,cluster,region_info}. Team-scoped via get_current_team.
reuse_map.ui_role: Top-level server nodes. For an ops panel you want ALL servers, so add a System-Manager variant that ignores the team filter (mirror get_dev_overview_benches' frappe.only_for('System Manager')).

reuse_map.ui_need: List all benches under each server (middle tier)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: every non-archived Bench enriched with server/group/cluster titles, site_count, status, last_commit. System-Manager whitelisted, batched (no N+1), already consumed by the built DevOverview Vue page.
reuse_map.ui_role: THE canonical bench enumerator. Group its rows by the server field to build the server→bench tree. (Do NOT use api.bench.all — that is keyed on Release Group, not physical Bench rows.)

reuse_map.ui_need: List sites under each bench (leaf tier / drill-down)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: {sites:[{name,status,host_name,scheduler_enabled,...}], recent_commits, build_history, errors:{count,errors}} for one bench. Already drives the DevOverview expand panel.
reuse_map.ui_role: On-expand loader for a bench node: shows its sites plus failed-Agent-Job error feed.

reuse_map.ui_need: Per-bench service status (web/workers/schedule/redis-cache/redis-queue/socketio/sshd/code-server up-down)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: list[SupervisorProcess]{program,name,status(Running/Stopped/Fatal/Exited),uptime,uptime_string,message,group,pid}. Whitelisted + @protected('Bench'). Returns [] unless bench status in (Active,Broken).
reuse_map.ui_role: THE per-service row source for each bench — covers redis, supervisor, sshd, workers as program rows. group_supervisor_processes/sort_supervisor_processes (bench.py) pre-nest them by category for the collapsible tree. This is a synchronous in-container exec (slow at scale) → call via the new aggregator with caching, not per-row on render.

reuse_map.ui_need: Disk service status (per server)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: get_storage_usage hits agent /server/storage-breakdown (per-mount/dir disk). usage/total_resource return {disk,memory,free_memory,vcpu} from Prometheus. StorageBreakdownDialog.vue already renders the breakdown.
reuse_map.ui_role: Disk chip + drill-down per server. get_storage_usage is already dashboard-callable. (Watch Tower's richer reclaimable/docker-df SCAN_CMD in check_server_disk_usage is a secondary, wrapper-only option if you want TEMP/APT/journal reclaimable detail.)

reuse_map.ui_need: Docker service status (per server)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: currently returns bool + emails; INTERNALLY builds issues=[{server,container,state,status}] from `docker ps -a` over SSH, but DROPS running containers and discards the dict into an email.
reuse_map.ui_role: Docker row per server. Reuse the SSH cmd + parse loop but REMOVE the unhealthy-only filter (board wants all containers) and RETURN the dict as JSON instead of emailing. Build inside the new Watch-Tower→JSON adapter.

reuse_map.ui_need: SSH service status (reachability dot per server)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: check_ssh_connectivity runs ssh_cmd('echo OK') per active tabServer (excludes press-ctrl), returns bool. ssh_cmd itself returns (success,stdout,stderr) and is reuse_as_is.
reuse_map.ui_role: Up/down SSH dot per server. Reuse ssh_cmd('echo OK') directly in the aggregator (cleanest reachability probe) and return success per server. get_bench_dev_info also gives the bench SSH ip+port (22000+offset) for the VS Code / ssh tile.

reuse_map.ui_need: Redis service status
reuse_map.where: press/api/bench.py:get_processes (redis-cache + redis-queue appear as supervisor program rows)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: redis-cache/redis-queue/socketio show up as SupervisorProcess rows with Running/Stopped status per bench — because in Press, redis runs as supervisor programs INSIDE each bench container, not as a host service.
reuse_map.ui_role: Redis status is just two service rows in the per-bench supervisor list — no separate probe needed. (Watch Tower's check_redis_health is press-ctrl-LOCAL-only PING/MISCONF and does NOT fan out per server, so it is NOT the right source for a per-bench board; skip it. There is no host-level redis in Press by design.)

reuse_map.ui_need: MariaDB service status + live activity
reuse_map.returns_or_does: ping_mariadb -> bool (swallows exceptions, safe for a status dot). get_db_processlist(site_name) -> [{id,user,time,state,query}] SHOW PROCESSLIST scoped to a site DB; kill_db_process kills one. ping_mariadb is @frappe.whitelist (desk-only).
reuse_map.ui_role: MariaDB up/down dot (ping_mariadb, needs a @dashboard_whitelist wrapper or fold into aggregator) + per-site drill-down (get_db_processlist + kill, already dashboard-callable & team-gated). NOTE: Watch Tower's check_mariadb_health connection-pool SQL is truncated/buggy — do NOT reuse that branch.

reuse_map.ui_need: Microservices health (Code Analysis / LiteLLM / Sanad Brain / MinIO etc.)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: probes a HARDCODED services list (only 'Code Analysis' http://localhost:8200/health) via ssh_cmd curl -sf, expects '"status":"ok"'; returns bool + emails.
reuse_map.ui_role: Microservices row. Externalize the hardcoded list into config/a doctype, return up/down + raw response as JSON. Press has NO doctype model for these services, so the catalog is partly new. Build inside the Watch-Tower→JSON adapter.

reuse_map.ui_need: Agent health (per server)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: agent_health(server) -> {verdict:healthy|slow|stuck|no_activity, recent_jobs:{by_status}, last_success_seconds_ago, running_jobs, undelivered_jobs} — pure Agent-Job DB derivation, fast, no SSH. ping_agent -> agent 'pong' (short timeout). Both @frappe.whitelist, NO dashboard wrapper.
reuse_map.ui_role: Agent-health column AND the restart safety gate. Add a press.api.server.check_agent_health wrapper (mirror the existing check_memory_pressure). REUSE its verdict to DISABLE the restart button when verdict=='slow' (server.py already uses this as _GATE_A_GUARDED_TOOLS). ping_agent feeds the green/red agent dot.

reuse_map.ui_need: Memory / host health (per server)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: {verdict:ok|elevated|critical, memory_total_mb, memory_available_mb, swap_used_pct, recent_oom_kills, _cached} — SSH/Ansible probe of /proc/meminfo, cached 60s/server. ALREADY surfaced on dashboard via ServerAdmin.vue.
reuse_map.ui_role: Memory verdict + free-MB tile per server. Use the existing check_memory_pressure wrapper as-is. Pair with press.api.server.analytics (ServerCharts.vue) for cpu/memory/load time-series.

reuse_map.ui_need: View a service's log (click service -> log drawer)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: logs() returns available log filenames per bench/site; get_log(log_type,doc_name,log_name) returns parsed entries with a per-type FORMATTER_MAP covering bench,worker,frappe,ipython,database,redis-cache,redis-queue,scheduler,web.error,monitor.json. All @frappe.whitelist+@protected. Reads via Agent HTTPS (not ssh).
reuse_map.ui_role: THE log drawer. Map each supervisor service row to its log file (redis-cache->redis-cache.log, worker->worker.log, etc.), then call get_log. The Vue trio LogBrowser/LogList/LogViewer.vue already renders this in a TanStack table with level+search — reuse LogViewer.vue verbatim as the drawer body.

reuse_map.ui_need: View live restart/deploy job progress + tracebacks (the 'why' behind a service action)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: agent_job_progress -> per-step live output_tail (Cursor-style); agent_job_traceback -> post-mortem output+traceback tail; bench_provision_progress -> chain[] timeline with derived stage. All @frappe.whitelist, NO dashboard wrapper/gate (built for MCP token auth).
reuse_map.ui_role: Poll agent_job_progress every 3-10s while a restart/deploy Agent Job runs to stream its log; agent_job_traceback for a failed action. Add @dashboard_whitelist wrappers or role checks before exposing to the Vue panel.

reuse_map.ui_need: Restart a whole bench
reuse_map.returns_or_does: creates an async 'Bench Restart' Agent Job restarting all supervisor programs. restart_bench_for_site -> Bench.restart_bench() is System-Manager-gated, logs the actor, and is ALREADY wired in DevOverview.restartBench() with confirmDialog. Bench.restart(web_only=True) restarts only gunicorn (near-zero-downtime).
reuse_map.ui_role: Per-bench Restart button. Reuse restart_bench_for_site (already dashboard-callable + audited) or the @protected api.bench.restart. Poll the returned Agent Job via agent_job_progress.

reuse_map.ui_need: Restart a SINGLE service (redis, one worker, scheduler)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: Bench.supervisorctl(action:'restart'|'start'|'stop'|..., programs=name|list) creates a 'Call Bench Supervisorctl' Agent Job targeting one program. Capability EXISTS but is NOT @frappe.whitelist / NOT @dashboard_whitelist — only server-side Python today.
reuse_map.ui_role: THE 'click a service -> restart it' action — the single most important missing wire. Add a ~3-line @frappe.whitelist+@protected('Bench') wrapper that VALIDATES action in {start,restart} (gate stop/remove/clear behind a stronger role) and validates the program name against get_processes output, then calls Bench(name).supervisorctl(action, programs=[name]).

reuse_map.ui_need: Restart the server (VM)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: hard-reboots the whole VM (AWS/OCI/DO/Hetzner only; NotImplementedError otherwise). @protected(['Server','Database Server']).
reuse_map.ui_role: Per-server 'Reboot' button. HIGH blast radius — wrap in confirmDialog + explicit System-Manager check + audit log. Already dashboard-exposed.

reuse_map.ui_need: Restart MariaDB engine (DB server)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: enqueues an Ansible 'restart_mysql.yml' playbook over SSH (NOT an Agent Job). @frappe.whitelist (NOT dashboard). HIGH risk — restarts DB for ALL sites on that server.
reuse_map.ui_role: DB-server 'Restart MariaDB' action behind a strong confirm + maintenance-window gate. Add a @protected/System-Manager wrapper before exposing.

reuse_map.ui_need: Restart the agent process
reuse_map.returns_or_does: pulls agent code AND bounces the agent process (closest proxy to 'restart agent'). @frappe.whitelist, not dashboard. There is NO pure 'just restart the agent' method — the documented path tells operators to SSH supervisorctl by hand.
reuse_map.ui_role: Agent restart button = update_agent (the reusable proxy). MUST call agent_health first and disable when verdict in {slow,stuck} to avoid corrupting a mid-migrate worker.

reuse_map.ui_need: Reload nginx / proxy config
reuse_map.returns_or_does: Agent(server).reload_nginx() — LOW risk (reload not restart). NOT whitelisted.
reuse_map.ui_role: Optional 'reload proxy' button; needs a whitelisted+@protected wrapper. Logic fully reusable.

reuse_map.ui_need: Service liveness dots (agent/mariadb/agent-job) before offering restart
reuse_map.returns_or_does: ping_agent->'pong' (2,5s timeout), ping_mariadb->bool, ping_agent_job->Ping Job name, ping_ansible->reachability. All @frappe.whitelist (desk-only).
reuse_map.ui_role: Green/red service dots per server. Wrap in (or fold into) the new aggregator with @dashboard_whitelist so the Vue board can call them.

reuse_map.ui_need: Single payload: full server -> bench -> service tree (the board feed)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: MISSING. get_dev_overview_benches gives benches but NOT their supervisor status; get_processes is one-bench-at-a-time synchronous container exec; host/disk/agent/memory live in 4-5 different methods. The UI would otherwise fan out N slow calls.
reuse_map.ui_role: NEW @dashboard_whitelist aggregator that fans out (parallel) over get_dev_overview_benches + get_processes per bench + check_memory_pressure/get_storage_usage/ping_* per server + the Watch-Tower JSON adapter, normalizes into one server->bench->service[] payload, and caches to a short Redis TTL. This is the central new piece.

reuse_map.ui_need: Status table with per-row colored badges + inline actions
reuse_map.returns_or_does: generic createListResource-backed table: columns declare type:'Badge' with a theme function of the row, filterControls, rowActions auto-bound to run_doc_method via a whitelistedMethods map.
reuse_map.ui_role: THE reusable service-row mechanism. A theme(status)=>green|red|orange|gray fn colors each service dot; rowActions wire restart. Add a 'Services' tab to server.js detail.tabs to get rows+badges+restart for near-free.

reuse_map.ui_need: Board page shell (summary cards + filter + expandable per-row tree)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: hand-built status board: summary cards, search/filter bar, per-bench table with status Badge, expandable panel, working Restart/dev/scheduler actions via run_doc_method. System-Manager gated. Bench-centric.
reuse_map.ui_role: Clone/extend as the new /infra-board page. Reuse layout + summary cards + expandable-row + Live badge wholesale; add the server tier on top and per-service rows. Restart action plumbing is already there.

reuse_map.ui_need: Logs / service drawer shell + confirm dialogs
reuse_map.where: dashboard/src/utils/components.jsx:confirmDialog / renderInDialog + GenericDialog.vue; LogViewer.vue for the body
reuse_map.returns_or_does: confirmDialog({title,message,onSuccess}) for destructive restarts (DevOverview already uses it); renderInDialog mounts any component; LogViewer.vue renders parsed log entries with level badges, search, sort, pagination.
reuse_map.ui_role: Restart confirmations + log drawer. NOTE: frappe-ui Dialog is centered/modal — a right-side drawer shell is a small custom add; LogViewer content itself is reuse_as_is.

reuse_map.ui_need: Action/data bridge from Vue to backend
reuse_map.returns_or_does: run_doc_method is the universal action bridge (no per-method endpoint needed) for any @whitelist/@dashboard_whitelist doc method; createResource gives reactive {data,loading,reload,submit} with optional polling.
reuse_map.ui_role: Wire all restart actions through run_doc_method; wire the aggregator/logs through createResource with .reload() on an interval for the 'Live' board.

reuse_map.ui_need: On-demand JSON status from Watch Tower host-level checks (disk reclaimable, docker, ssh, redis, mariadb, microservice)
reuse_map.where: n/a (every check_* returns bool and emails; structured dicts are computed then discarded)
reuse_map.returns_or_does: MISSING as JSON. Watch Tower checks are an ALERT engine — none are @frappe.whitelist, none return JSON, several are press-ctrl-LOCAL-only and don't fan out per server, and calling them directly would also burn the should_send_alert throttle and SEND emails.
reuse_map.ui_role: NEW read-only status adapter that REUSES the primitives (ssh_cmd, get_all_servers, the SCAN_CMD / docker-ps / curl-health logic) but RETURNS dicts, removes unhealthy-only filters, fans LOCAL probes out per server, and never calls send_alert_email/should_send_alert. Feeds the docker/ssh/microservice rows of the aggregator.

gaps.missing: Whitelisted per-service restart endpoint. Bench.supervisorctl(action, programs) (press/press/doctype/bench/bench.py) can restart a single supervisor program but is not whitelisted. Need a @frappe.whitelist+@protected('Bench') wrapper that validates action in {start,restart} and the program name against get_processes output before calling supervisorctl(programs=[name]).
gaps.why_needed: This is the literal 'click the service to restart it' requirement. Without it the panel can only restart the whole bench, not just redis or one worker.

gaps.missing: Single batched server->bench->service aggregator endpoint (@dashboard_whitelist get_infra_tree). Must fan out get_dev_overview_benches + per-bench get_processes + per-server check_memory_pressure/get_storage_usage/ping_* + the Watch-Tower JSON adapter, in parallel, normalize to one payload, and cache to a short Redis TTL.
gaps.why_needed: No aggregate exists today; the UI would otherwise make N synchronous in-container supervisorctl-status execs (slow at scale) plus 4-5 scattered health calls per server on every refresh.

gaps.missing: Watch-Tower-checks -> JSON status adapter. Re-expose check_docker_container_health (drop unhealthy-only filter), check_ssh_connectivity, check_microservice_health (externalize the hardcoded service list), and optionally check_server_disk_usage reclaimable detail as read-only JSON that RETURNS the internal dicts, fans LOCAL-only probes out per server via ssh_cmd, and never emails or touches should_send_alert.
gaps.why_needed: Watch Tower has the best SSH probes + thresholds for docker/ssh/microservice/disk-reclaimable, but every check_* returns only a bool and emails as a side effect — unusable by a live board as-is. check_mariadb_health's connection-pool SQL is also truncated/buggy and must be rewritten or skipped.

gaps.missing: Dashboard wrappers + role gates for the ungated MCP/ping methods: agent_health, agent_job_progress, agent_job_traceback, bench_provision_progress, site_status, deploy_candidate_status, lock.status (all @frappe.whitelist, no dashboard wrapper, no team-access gate — built for MCP token auth) and ping_agent/ping_mariadb/ping_agent_job/ping_ansible (@frappe.whitelist desk-only). Add press.api.server.check_agent_health mirroring the existing check_memory_pressure pattern, and @dashboard_whitelist (or System-Manager) wrappers for the rest.
gaps.why_needed: Calling deploy_flow.* directly from the Vue dashboard runs them as the session user WITHOUT a team-access check; the ping_* are not in the dashboard allowlist at all. They power agent health, job-progress log streaming, and service dots, so they must be safely exposed.

gaps.missing: Server->bench->service tree page in the Vue dashboard (clone of DevOverview.vue) + a per-service-row component (generalize BenchWatchStatus.vue health-pill, or a 'service' ObjectList config object) + a right-side drawer shell (frappe-ui Dialog is centered-only).
gaps.why_needed: DevOverview is bench-centric and has no server tier, no per-service rows, and no side drawer. The table/badge/expand mechanics are reusable but the server>bench>service grouping/aggregation UI layer is new.

gaps.missing: Live auto-refresh / caching layer. DevOverview shows a 'Live' badge but only refreshes on manual click. Add createResource .reload() on a 5-15s interval (or wire socket.js realtime), and back the aggregator with a short Redis TTL so polling does not re-run a synchronous supervisorctl-status exec per bench every tick.
gaps.why_needed: The operator asked for a LIVE panel; without caching, frequent polling of N benches' container execs is too slow and load-heavy.

gaps.missing: Server / host-level system logs (journalctl, /var/log, systemctl status, docker daemon, standalone /var/log/mysql/error.log on dedicated DB servers) have NO whitelisted accessor — only Server.ansible_run (internal SSH, no whitelist) exists. A new role-gated wrapper with a FIXED command allowlist is needed if the drawer must show host/daemon logs beyond bench files.
gaps.why_needed: log_browser.get_log only covers bench/site files written into the bench logs/ dir. A custom microservice or a daemon-level error log (nginx/redis/mysql on a dedicated server) has no path today.

gaps.missing: Microservices catalog. Press has NO doctype model for non-supervisor sidecar services (LiteLLM, Sanad Brain, MinIO, Code Analysis). check_microservice_health hardcodes a single service. A small config doctype (or settings list) of {name,url,server} is needed to drive the microservices row.
gaps.why_needed: The board must list arbitrary microservices per server; there is no data source to enumerate them today.

result.architecture_markdown:
## Recommended architecture — maximize reuse, minimize new build

### 1. Page placement
Add a new System-Manager-gated route `/infra-board` in `dashboard/src/pages/` by **cloning `DevOverview.vue`** (it is already the target board: summary cards + filter bar + expandable per-row table + working restart actions via `run_doc_method`). Add a **server tier above benches** and **per-service rows below**. Reuse its `confirmDialog` restart plumbing and `buildBadgeClass()`/`ObjectListCell` Badge-theme mechanism unchanged. Generalize `BenchWatchStatus.vue` into a per-service health pill, or define a `'service'` config object for `ObjectList.vue` to get rows+badges+restart for near-free.

### 2. Data feed — ONE new aggregator, everything else reused
Build a single `@dashboard_whitelist get_infra_tree()` (the central new piece) that fans out, in parallel, and normalizes into a `server -> benches[] -> services[]` payload:
- **Servers**: `press.api.server.all` (add a System-Manager variant that ignores the team filter).
- **Benches**: `bench_dev_overview.get_dev_overview_benches` (as-is) grouped by its `server` field.
- **Per-bench services**: `press.api.bench.get_processes` -> `Bench.supervisorctl_status` -> `parse_supervisor_status` (the 8 supervisor programs incl. redis-cache/redis-queue/socketio/sshd). Pre-group with `group_supervisor_processes` / `sort_supervisor_processes`.
- **Per-server host services**: `press.api.server.check_memory_pressure` (host_memory_pressure, 60s cached) for memory; `Server.get_storage_usage` (@dashboard_whitelist) + `press.api.server.usage`/`analytics` for disk/cpu/load; `ping_mariadb`/`ping_agent`/`ping_agent_job`/`ping_ansible` for mariadb/agent/ssh dots; `deploy_flow.agent_health` (via a new `check_agent_health` wrapper) for the agent verdict.
- **Docker / ssh / microservice rows**: the new **Watch-Tower->JSON adapter** that reuses `_helpers.ssh_cmd` + `get_all_servers` + the exact SCAN_CMD / `docker ps -a` / curl-`/health` logic from `check_docker_container_health` / `check_ssh_connectivity` / `check_microservice_health`, but RETURNS dicts (no `send_alert_email`, no `should_send_alert`, no unhealthy-only filter, LOCAL probes fanned out per server). Skip `check_mariadb_health`'s truncated connection-pool SQL.

### 3. On-demand vs polled
- `supervisorctl_status` / `get_processes` are **synchronous in-container execs** (slow at scale) and `ssh_cmd` probes have up-to-30s timeouts. So: the aggregator caches results to a **short Redis TTL (~10-20s)**; the Vue page polls `get_infra_tree()` via `createResource.reload()` on a **5-15s interval** (DevOverview's manual-refresh becomes auto). `host_memory_pressure` already self-caches 60s. For an in-flight restart/deploy, **poll `agent_job_progress` every 3-10s** (it reads Agent Job rows, cheap) until the job leaves Running — this drives the live log/progress stream. No websocket needed for v1 (socket.js exists if a true push board is wanted later).

### 4. Logs drawer
Reuse the existing trio `LogBrowser/LogList/LogViewer.vue` and its backend `press.api.bench.logs` (file list) + `press.api.log_browser.get_log(log_type, doc_name, log_name)` (parsed, per-type FORMATTER_MAP covers bench/worker/frappe/database/scheduler/redis-cache/redis-queue/web.error). **Map each supervisor service row to its log file** (redis-cache->redis-cache.log, worker->worker.log, scheduler->scheduler.log) and call `get_log` on click; render with `LogViewer.vue` (level badges + search + pagination) inside a right-side drawer shell (small custom add since frappe-ui Dialog is centered-only). For a failed restart/deploy use `agent_job_traceback`. Host/daemon logs (journalctl, /var/log/mysql) are a gap — only `Server.ansible_run` exists, ungated; build a fixed-command-allowlist wrapper if needed.

### 5. Restart actions -> existing endpoints
- **Restart bench** -> `restart_bench_for_site` -> `Bench.restart_bench()` (already dashboard-callable, System-Manager-gated, audited; wired in `DevOverview.restartBench` with confirmDialog). Use `Bench.restart(web_only=True)` for near-zero-downtime web-only.
- **Restart one service** -> NEW ~3-line `@frappe.whitelist+@protected('Bench')` wrapper around `Bench.supervisorctl(action, programs=[name])`, restricting action to {start,restart} and validating the program name against `get_processes`.
- **Reboot server (VM)** -> `press.api.server.reboot` (as-is, HIGH risk, confirm + System-Manager + audit).
- **Restart MariaDB** -> `database_server.restart_mariadb` (HIGH risk, Ansible, confirm + maintenance window).
- **Restart agent** -> `Server.update_agent` (the only proxy; gate on `agent_health` verdict).
All wired through `press.api.client.run_doc_method`. **Safety gate**: call `agent_health`/`agent_job_progress` and **disable restart buttons when verdict in {slow,stuck}** — Press already uses this as `_GATE_A_GUARDED_TOOLS` to prevent corrupting a mid-migrate worker. Use `press.api.lock.status` to grey-out actions on a locked Site/Release Group.

### 6. Permission / security model (admin-only infra controls)
- **Page + aggregator**: `frappe.only_for('System Manager')` (match `get_dev_overview_benches`) — these are global ops controls, not team-scoped.
- **Convention**: call the `@protected` `api/*.py` wrappers (team/permission enforced) and expose new methods via `@dashboard_whitelist` or an explicit System-Manager check — never expose raw `Bench.docker_execute`, `Server.ansible_run`, or `ssh_cmd` to the client.
- **ssh_cmd contract**: commands MUST be hardcoded literals — the per-service restart and any host-log wrapper must whitelist a FIXED command/program set and validate identifiers against known data (get_processes program names, get_all_servers ips), never pass free-form user input.
- **Audit + confirm**: add an activity-log entry and a `confirmDialog` for every high-blast-radius action (VM reboot, MariaDB restart, agent restart, update-all-sites). Do NOT expose `bench.update`/`update_all_sites`/`site.migrate` as one-click buttons.
- **Throttle**: the read-only status path must bypass Watch Tower's `should_send_alert` entirely so a UI refresh never burns alert budget or sends emails.
